statement_record.book: Exercise 4.5.i: verify that the category Ω^X of predicates on a set X is cartesian closed, with conjunction p ∧ q = ∃_i Δ_i r and implication q ⇒ r = ∀_i Δ_i r computed from the quantifier adjoint triple ∃_i ⊣ Δ_i ⊣ ∀_i associated to the monomorphism i : Q >-> X naming a predicate's truth set.
statement_record.intree: Props (Instance/Props.v) is the thin category of propositions ordered by implication; Props_Cartesian makes conjunction the binary product and Props_Closed makes implication the exponential, exp_iso being the currying bijection Hom(R ∧ P, Q) ≅ Hom(R, P → Q).
statement_record.strength_comparison: intree-weaker: only the UNINDEXED truth-value case is covered — Props is Ω itself (equivalently Ω^1, the fibre over a point), a Heyting prealgebra whose ∧ and ⇒ are given DIRECTLY as Coq's `and` and `impl`, not derived from any quantifier adjunction. The exercise's actual content — the X-indexed category of predicates and the derivation of ∧ and ⇒ from ∃_i ⊣ Δ_i ⊣ ∀_i — is not present.
